title: GTM Ramp Logistics & KPI Stitchbook
content:
Purpose: living stitchbook for planning the next GTM ramp (pilot → regional → global). Focus is operational sequencing, KPI guardrails, and minimal viable contingency playbooks. Work-in-progress: half-structured notes, assumptions, open questions.

Top-level objectives (what success looks like for this ramp):
- stable 99th pct latency under 350ms for 95% of requests (hosted tier)
- <15% SLA burn for Dedicated customers during surge windows
- adoption: 3 pilot customers converted to paid within 60 days post-beta
- cost: unit inference cost within projected budget (target $0.004/token equivalent)

Critical constraints to track:
- Dedicated capacity lead time: 6 weeks minimum for reserve GPU pool allocation
- Private deployment security review SLA: 21 business days for legal & infosec signoff
- Observability retention tier toggle impacts: +20% storage costs (estimate)

Assumptions (call out so we revisit as data arrives):
- prefix caching will reduce token cost by ~12% for conversational flows (based on internal evals)
- average sequence length 120 tokens for core use case (product search assistant)
- default batch size target 32 for mid-SLA throughput windows

KPI tracker (rolling, update weekly):
- Traffic: requests/min (baseline pilot 50 rpm → ramp to 1,500 rpm regional)
- Error rate: 5xx % (target <0.3%)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 (ms)
- Cost per 1k tokens equivalent (USD)
- KV cache hit rate (%)
- Canary failover count (events)
- Customer activation time (days from sign-up to first production call)

Quick tracker table (placeholders — replace with live metrics):
- week 0 (pilot): traffic 50 rpm, error 0.2%, p95 280ms, cost $1.8/1k
- week 2: traffic 320 rpm, error 0.35%, p95 340ms, cost $1.6/1k
- week 4: traffic 900 rpm, error 0.5% (incidents), p95 410ms, cost $1.2/1k

Launch readiness checklist (Pilot → Regional → Global), condensed operational steps:
1) Pilot sign-off (owner: product-ops)
   - Confirm pilot success criteria met (adoption + latency + error window).
   - Exec check-in: product + eng + SRE (meeting notes attach CONF-12345).
   - Legal: data processing agreement countersigned if customer PII involved.

2) Platform readiness (owner: eng-sre / serving-runtime)
   - Autoscaling policy validated with synthetic surge test (JIRA-OPS-8472).
   - Circuit breaker and fallback model variants configured (fallback policy: small-quantized model).
   - Metrics dashboard: token-level cost & per-route latency deck ready for oncall.

3) Observability & Alerts (owner: observability)
   - Alert thresholds: error >0.5% sustained 5m, p95 >500ms sustained 10m.
   - Playbook pages linked to alerts with runbooks (see linked_artifacts).

4) Capacity & Billing (owner: product-ops + finance)
   - Reserve capacity commitments executed for Dedicated where needed.
   - Price guardrails communicated to sales and CS (margin impact analysis attached).

5) Customer success readiness (owner: customer-success)
   - Onboarding checklist: SDK keys, example prompts, test harness.
   - Escalation channel: triage Slack channel #pilot-ramp and 24/7 rotation oncall.

Contingency plays (short form):
- If p95 latency spikes >25% during ramp: throttled rollout (pause new customer invites), enable prefix-cache warmup, increase burst capacity for 72h.
- If cost per token deviates >30% above plan: switch affected routes to quantized variants, engage Optimize team for batching adjustments.
- If Dedicated pool unhealthy (>3 node failures in 1h): auto-failover to hosted fallback model and notify account owners.

Open questions / blockers (needs owners):
- Can infra compress retention at metric level for longer SLI history without blowing costs? (Owner: observability)
- What's the exact turnaround for legal on non-standard DPA terms for EU pilot? (Owner: legal)
- Capacity forecast mismatch with sales pipeline — who owns the cushion policy? (Owner: finance + product)

Mini runbook snippets (copy/paste ready):
- Surge immediate: add 10% burst cap via infra console → monitor p95/p99 for 15m → if stable, keep; if not, enact fallback model route mapping.
- Incident comms: short blurb for status page (SRE) + customer-impact note for CS with next steps and ETA.

Signals to stop the ramp (abort criteria):
- Sustained SLA burn >15% over 24h for Dedicated customers
- More than two sev2 incidents impacting >30% customers in 48h
- Legal block preventing needed contractual terms

Next 90-day milestones (high level):
- Week 0–4: pilot expansion (3 pilot customers), finalize canary policies, run two synthetic surge tests
- Week 5–8: regional rollout to 5 markets, extra observability retention for regional traces
- Week 9–12: scalable billing contracts for Dedicated, begin Private deployment onboarding for 1 customer

Notes + quick links: this doc is intentionally terse — refer to CONF-12345 for full rollout deck and JIRA-OPS-8472 for infra tickets. Slack thread: #pilot-ramp (pinned messages).

TODOs (short):
- [ ] finalize prefix-cache configuration and validate with sample of prod traffic (owner: serving-runtime, due 2024-11-29)
- [ ] legal sign DPA for EU pilot (owner: legal, due 2024-12-06)
- [ ] run cost-sensitivity sim with Optimize (owner: product-ops + optimize, due 2024-12-03)
- [ ] prepare customer-facing onboarding one-pager (owner: customer-success, due 2024-11-22)

Retro notes (from pilot learnings):
- Early assumption: batching would always reduce cost. Reality: with low seq length, batching benefits drop off; need dynamic batch sizing.
- Observability gaps: token attribution per route incomplete — add a middleware tag to align billing vs cost dashboards.

Author note: keep this file as a single-source-of-truth sprint stitchbook for the immediate ramp. Move completed sections into the canonical go-to-prod decks and playbooks.

Revision history: 2024-11-15 initial draft (Maya Chen). 2024-12-03 cost sim notes added (Noah). 2025-01-10 regional rollout cadence updated (Lena).
